The Omnibus amendment also extends the application date for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028.
One source states the extended transition for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products runs until 2 August 2027, rather than 2028.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date Annex III high-risk AI system obligations would apply, but this deadline has since been extended to 2 December 2027 through the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) amendment (high confidence). Related obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) have similarly been pushed to 2 August 2028 (high confidence), though some ambiguity remains over whether these dates are fixed or conditional on regulatory readiness.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). A European Parliament summary, however, describes a 36-month timeline from entry into force (roughly August 2027), creating an unresolved discrepancy with the more commonly cited 24-month/August 2026 figure (medium confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) amended the Act's timeline, extending the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). The same amendment extended the deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Squire Patton Boggs AI Timeline](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf). One source cites 2 August 2027 instead of 2028 for Annex I systems, an outlier not corroborated elsewhere (low confidence) [Snowflake EU AI Act](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act).

Political agreement on the Omnibus between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The Commission's Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, with the resulting Regulation entering into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

### Conditional vs. Fixed Dates
The Commission's original Omnibus proposal suggested adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that high-risk rules would only apply once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and compliance tools were available—implying a conditional rather than fixed date (medium confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). Some secondary sources assert the final text fixed 2 December 2027 as a firm statutory deadline tied to a "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," though this specific legal citation is not confirmed by an official EUR-Lex source in the data reviewed (low confidence) [EU AI Act timeline and planning dates](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html), [AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

### Transitional and Grandfathering Provisions
The consolidated EUR-Lex text and official guidance indicate that high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 are only subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111).

### Pre-Omnibus Commentary
Several commentary pieces published before the Omnibus took effect continued to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting outdated information now superseded by the amendment (low confidence) [RAIL compliance countdown](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants guide](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Pre- vs. post-Omnibus dates**: Sources reflecting the original 2024 text cite 2 August 2026, while post-Omnibus sources cite 2 December 2027 for Annex III obligations — this is a timeline that changed via amendment, not a factual conflict per se.
- **24-month vs. 36-month original timeline**: The European Parliament's 36-month figure conflicts with the more widely cited 24-month/August 2026 date, unresolved in the available data (flagged below 0.4 confidence in underlying claim).
- **Annex I date discrepancy**: Most sources cite 2 August 2028 for Annex I-embedded systems, but one source states 2 August 2027 (low confidence, below 0.4).
- **Legal citation uncertainty**: "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is referenced by secondary sources but lacks confirmation via an official EUR-Lex citation (low confidence, below 0.4).
- **Fixed vs. conditional date**: Whether 2 December 2027 is a hard deadline or contingent on Commission confirmation of available standards remains unresolved.

## Knowledge Gaps
- The official, citable legal reference and adoption date for the Omnibus Regulation that sets the 2 December 2027 date is not fully confirmed.
- Whether the Commission retains discretion to further delay Annex III obligations pending standards readiness is unclear.
- The reason for the 2027-vs-2028 discrepancy on Annex I deadlines is unexplained.
- Further primary-source verification (official EUR-Lex publication of the amending Regulation) is needed to resolve timeline inconsistencies.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date Annex III high-risk AI system obligations would apply, but this deadline has since been extended to 2 December 2027 through the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) amendment (high confidence). Related obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) have similarly been pushed to 2 August 2028 (high confidence), though some ambiguity remains over whether these dates are fixed or conditional on regulatory readiness.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). A European Parliament summary, however, describes a 36-month timeline from entry into force (roughly August 2027), creating an unresolved discrepancy with the more commonly cited 24-month/August 2026 figure (medium confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) amended the Act's timeline, extending the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). The same amendment extended the deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Squire Patton Boggs AI Timeline](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf). One source cites 2 August 2027 instead of 2028 for Annex I systems, an outlier not corroborated elsewhere (low confidence) [Snowflake EU AI Act](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act).

Political agreement on the Omnibus between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The Commission's Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, with the resulting Regulation entering into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

### Conditional vs. Fixed Dates
The Commission's original Omnibus proposal suggested adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that high-risk rules would only apply once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and compliance tools were available—implying a conditional rather than fixed date (medium confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). Some secondary sources assert the final text fixed 2 December 2027 as a firm statutory deadline tied to a "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," though this specific legal citation is not confirmed by an official EUR-Lex source in the data reviewed (low confidence) [EU AI Act timeline and planning dates](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html), [AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

### Transitional and Grandfathering Provisions
The consolidated EUR-Lex text and official guidance indicate that high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 are only subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111).

### Pre-Omnibus Commentary
Several commentary pieces published before the Omnibus took effect continued to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting outdated information now superseded by the amendment (low confidence) [RAIL compliance countdown](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants guide](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Pre- vs. post-Omnibus dates**: Sources reflecting the original 2024 text cite 2 August 2026, while post-Omnibus sources cite 2 December 2027 for Annex III obligations — this is a timeline that changed via amendment, not a factual conflict per se.
- **24-month vs. 36-month original timeline**: The European Parliament's 36-month figure conflicts with the more widely cited 24-month/August 2026 date, unresolved in the available data (flagged below 0.4 confidence in underlying claim).
- **Annex I date discrepancy**: Most sources cite 2 August 2028 for Annex I-embedded systems, but one source states 2 August 2027 (low confidence, below 0.4).
- **Legal citation uncertainty**: "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is referenced by secondary sources but lacks confirmation via an official EUR-Lex citation (low confidence, below 0.4).
- **Fixed vs. conditional date**: Whether 2 December 2027 is a hard deadline or contingent on Commission confirmation of available standards remains unresolved.

## Knowledge Gaps
- The official, citable legal reference and adoption date for the Omnibus Regulation that sets the 2 December 2027 date is not fully confirmed.
- Whether the Commission retains discretion to further delay Annex III obligations pending standards readiness is unclear.
- The reason for the 2027-vs-2028 discrepancy on Annex I deadlines is unexplained.
- Further primary-source verification (official EUR-Lex publication of the amending Regulation) is needed to resolve timeline inconsistencies.
